top_temples.name: Sant Dnyaneshwar Maharaj Samadhi Mandir
top_temples.deity: Samadhi shrine of Sant Dnyaneshwar, under a Siddheshwar (Shiva) shrine
top_temples.location_note: Built 1570; Dnyaneshwar, 13th-century Marathi saint-poet, took sanjeevan samadhi here. Major Varkari pilgrimage centre on the Indrayani river.

top_temples.name: Vitthal-Rukmini Temple
top_temples.location_note: Located within Alandi town near the Dnyaneshwar Samadhi Mandir; a distinct shrine central to the town's Varkari worship tradition.

top_temples.name: Nagnath (Nageshwar) Jyotirlinga Temple
top_temples.location_note: In Hingoli district; one of the twelve Jyotirlingas of Shiva, a major pan-India pilgrimage site.

top_temples.name: Subsidiary Jyotirlinga Shrines, Nagnath Temple Complex
top_temples.deity: Shiva (represented as the other eleven Jyotirlingas)
top_temples.location_note: The complex houses 12 mini shrines replicating the other Jyotirlingas plus 108 smaller temples; used here as the town's second entry since it is defined by this single major shrine complex.

top_temples.name: Grishneshwar Jyotirlinga Temple
top_temples.location_note: Verul village, about 29 km from Aurangabad, near Ellora Caves; the twelfth and final Jyotirlinga, 13th-century, UNESCO-listed.

top_temples.name: Kailasa (Kailashanatha) Temple, Ellora
top_temples.location_note: Cave 16 of the Ellora Caves near Aurangabad; the world's largest monolithic rock-cut temple structure.

top_temples.name: Khandoba Temple
top_temples.location_note: Aurangabad; originally built in the 16th century by the Peshwas in Hemadpanthi style, later restored by the Holkars.

top_temples.name: Bhadra Maruti Temple
top_temples.location_note: About 4 km from Ellora Caves, Aurangabad district; notable for its reclining Hanuman idol.

top_temples.name: Omkareshwar Mahadev Mandir
top_temples.location_note: Aurangabad; a cluster-temple campus centred on the main Omkareshwar shrine.

top_temples.name: Bhimashankar Jyotirlinga Temple
top_temples.location_note: In the Sahyadri hills near Pune; one of the twelve Jyotirlingas, also the source region of the Bhima river.

top_temples.name: Gupt Bhimashankar
top_temples.location_note: A separate, older sacred site near the main Bhimashankar temple, associated with the origin legend of the Bhima river.

top_temples.name: Sant Tukaram Maharaj Janm Sthan / Sansthan Mandir
top_temples.location_note: Dehu village, Pune district; built 1723 CE on the site associated with the saint-poet Tukaram's life, a major Varkari pilgrimage site.

top_temples.name: Sant Tukaram Maharaj Gatha Mandir
top_temples.deity: Memorial shrine to Sant Tukaram's teachings
top_temples.location_note: Adjacent to the main Dehu shrine on the Indrayani river; walls inscribed with over 4,000 of Tukaram's devotional abhangs.

top_temples.name: Shree Ganpatipule Mandir (Swayambhu Ganapati Temple)
top_temples.location_note: Coastal Ratnagiri district; a roughly 400-year-old self-manifested (swayambhu) Ganesh idol facing the Arabian Sea, a major Konkan pilgrimage site.

top_temples.name: Ganeshgule (Agargule) Temple
top_temples.location_note: About 4 km away on the Pavas-Poorngad road; local legend holds the deity transferred itself from here to Ganpatipule, making it a closely linked second shrine.

top_temples.name: Omkareshwar Temple
top_temples.location_note: On Jai Nagar Road in the heart of Jalgaon city; a well-known local Shiva shrine.

top_temples.name: Iccha Devi Mandir
top_temples.location_note: Jalgaon city; several hundred years old.

top_temples.name: Shree Ram Mandir
top_temples.location_note: Jalgaon city; one of the more prominent Rama temples in the area.

top_temples.name: Shree Kshetra Padmalaya
top_temples.location_note: About 30 km from Jalgaon; one of India's 'two and a half' Ganpati peeths (ardha peeth).

top_temples.name: Patnadevi (Chandikadevi) Temple
top_temples.location_note: Jalgaon district; set amid scenic hill landscapes.

top_temples.name: Mahalaxmi Temple (Ambabai Temple)
top_temples.location_note: On the Panchganga river in Kolhapur; a Shakti Peetha, built in the 7th century during the Chalukya period, the city's defining shrine.

top_temples.name: Jyotiba Temple
top_temples.location_note: About 3,200 feet altitude near Kolhapur; founded around 1600s by Ranoji Shinde.

top_temples.name: Temblai Mandir
top_temples.location_note: Hilltop in eastern Kolhapur; a form of Renuka Devi/Durga.

top_temples.name: Uttareshwar Mahadev Temple
top_temples.location_note: On the banks of the Rankala River in Kolhapur.

top_temples.name: Bhavani Mandap
top_temples.location_note: Close to the Mahalaxmi Temple in central Kolhapur.

top_temples.name: Siddheshwar Ratneshwar Mandir
top_temples.location_note: 12th-century temple built by King Tamradwaj in Latur; draws a large fair during Mahashivratri.

top_temples.name: Shri Ashtavinayak Mandir
top_temples.location_note: Latur city; South Indian-style temple with a 9-ft Shiva statue and eight Ganesha idols in landscaped grounds.

top_temples.name: Shri Virat Hanuman Mandir
top_temples.location_note: Latur city; known for a 25-ft Hanuman statue and a water-curtain feature at the shrine.

top_temples.name: Jagdamba Mata Temple, Ganj Golai
top_temples.location_note: In Latur's Ganj Golai area, built in the Rashtrakuta era; a local Devi shrine tied to the regional Tulja Bhavani devotional tradition, distinct from the Tuljapur temple itself.

top_temples.name: Ganpati Mandir, Latur
top_temples.location_note: A locally prominent Ganesh shrine within Latur city.

top_temples.name: Siddhivinayak Temple
top_temples.location_note: Prabhadevi, Mumbai; founded 1801, among the most-visited and wealthiest temples in India.

top_temples.name: Mahalakshmi Temple
top_temples.location_note: Built 1831 by a Hindu merchant; sea-facing temple, a key Mumbai landmark.

top_temples.name: Babulnath Temple
top_temples.location_note: Malabar region of Mumbai, near Marine Lines; architecture evokes Kailash Parbat.

top_temples.name: Walkeshwar Temple
top_temples.location_note: Malabar Hill, Mumbai; built by the Silhara dynasty over a thousand years ago, tied to a Ramayana legend.

top_temples.name: Swaminarayan Temple
top_temples.location_note: Mumbai; over 100 years old, known for its carved pillars and three spires.

top_temples.name: Shri Ganesh Tekdi Mandir (Tekdicha Ganpati)
top_temples.location_note: Near Nagpur railway station; a centuries-old hilltop Ganesh shrine, one of the city's oldest temples.

top_temples.name: BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir
top_temples.location_note: Nagpur; the largest Swaminarayan temple among over 1,000 built by the Swaminarayan Sanstha worldwide.

top_temples.name: Shri Balaji Shri Karthikeya Temple
top_temples.location_note: Seminary Hills along Telankhedi Lake, Nagpur; modeled on the Tirupati Balaji temple.

top_temples.name: Sai Baba Temple
top_temples.location_note: Goswami Tulsidas Road, Nagpur.

top_temples.name: Koradi Temple
top_temples.location_note: About 15 km from Nagpur in Koradi; one of the 51 Shakti Peethas, idol believed self-manifested (swayambhu).

top_temples.name: Kalaram Temple
top_temples.location_note: Panchavati area of Nashik; built 1794 by Sardar Rangarao Odhekar, one of Maharashtra's most revered Rama temples.

top_temples.name: Saptashrungi Devi Mandir
top_temples.location_note: Atop a 1,230-m cliff near Nanduri village, Nashik district; one of the 'three-and-a-half' Shakti Peethas of Maharashtra.

top_temples.name: Someshwar Temple
top_temples.location_note: On the banks of the Godavari river in Nashik city; regarded as one of the holiest Shiva shrines in the city, distinct from Trimbakeshwar.

top_temples.name: Sita Gufaa (Sita Cave) Temple
top_temples.location_note: Panchavati, near Kalaram Temple, Nashik.

top_temples.name: Kapaleshwar Temple
top_temples.location_note: One of Nashik's oldest and most important temples, on the Godavari riverbank.

top_temples.name: Shri Vitthal Rukmini Temple
top_temples.location_note: Pandharpur's central shrine, called the 'Southern Kashi'; site of the massive annual Ashadi Ekadashi Wari pilgrimage.

top_temples.name: Pundalik Temple
top_temples.location_note: About 1 km from the main Vitthal temple in Pandharpur; dedicated to the legendary devotee credited with bringing Vitthal to the town.

top_temples.name: Shri Vaijnath (Vaidyanath) Jyotirlinga Temple
top_temples.location_note: Beed district; one of the twelve Jyotirlingas, built during the Yadava dynasty (12th-13th century), renovated by Ahilyabai Holkar in the 18th century.

top_temples.name: Parvati and Ganesha Sub-shrines, Vaijnath Temple Complex
top_temples.location_note: Subsidiary shrines within the same Vaijnath temple complex; used here as the town's second entry since no separate standalone major temple exists distinct to Parli itself.

top_temples.name: Dagdusheth Halwai Ganpati Temple
top_temples.location_note: Built 1893 in Pune; one of the most famous Ganpati temples in India, visited by over a hundred thousand pilgrims annually.

top_temples.name: Omkareshwar Temple
top_temples.location_note: On the banks of the Mutha river, Pune; built during the Peshwa regime.

top_temples.name: Shri Chatushrungi Devi Temple
top_temples.location_note: Pune; built during Shivaji Maharaj's reign, a 90-ft temple reached via 100 steps.

top_temples.name: Sarasbaug Ganpati Temple
top_temples.location_note: Pune; dates to the Peshwa era.

top_temples.name: Laxmi Narasimha Temple
top_temples.location_note: Pune; known for its black-stone architecture.

top_temples.name: Ganapati Temple (Bagetala Ganpati)
top_temples.location_note: Built 1843 by Thorle Chintamanrao Patwardhan in Sangli; guardian deity of the city, known for its black stone architecture.

top_temples.name: Sangameshwar Temple
top_temples.location_note: At the confluence of the Krishna and Warna rivers near Sangli; Chalukya-era temple.

top_temples.name: Bahubali Hill Temple
top_temples.location_note: A prominent Jain hill shrine near Sangli.

top_temples.name: Jwala Narsimh Temple
top_temples.location_note: Sangli; named for an eternal flame believed to burn naturally in the sanctum.

top_temples.name: Mahalaxmi Temple
top_temples.location_note: One of Sangli's most popular Devi temples.

top_temples.name: Shani Shingnapur Temple
top_temples.location_note: Shingnapur village, Ahmednagar district; open-air shrine with a self-manifested black stone idol, famous for the village's tradition of doorless houses.

top_temples.name: Dattatray Shrine, Shani Shingnapur Complex
top_temples.location_note: A subsidiary shrine within the same temple precinct, alongside the tomb of Saint Udasi Baba; used here as the town's second entry since Shingnapur's identity centers on the single Shani shrine.

top_temples.name: Shri Sai Baba Samadhi Mandir
top_temples.location_note: Shirdi's central shrine, established 1922; one of India's most-visited pilgrimage sites, complex includes Dwarkamai and Chavadi.

top_temples.name: Khandoba Temple
top_temples.location_note: In Shirdi town; the shrine where, per tradition, the teenage Sai Baba was first welcomed to Shirdi.

top_temples.name: Siddheshwar Temple
top_temples.location_note: Heart of Solapur city; Siddheshwar is the Gramdaivat (guardian deity) of Solapur, Hemadpanthi-style, believed built during the Yadava dynasty.

top_temples.name: Rukmini Temple
top_temples.location_note: One of the oldest and most revered temples in Solapur, dedicated to Krishna's consort.

top_temples.name: Shri Venkateshwara Devasthanam
top_temples.location_note: A well-known Vishnu temple within Solapur city.

top_temples.name: Sri Markandeya Mandir
top_temples.location_note: A notable temple within Solapur city.

top_temples.name: Swami Samarth Temple, Akkalkot
top_temples.location_note: Akkalkot, about 38 km from Solapur city within Solapur district; built around an ancient banyan tree.

top_temples.name: Trimbakeshwar Shiva Temple
top_temples.location_note: Trimbak town, Nashik district; one of the twelve Jyotirlingas, unique for its three-faced lingam, built mid-18th century by Peshwa Nana Saheb, and the source of the Godavari river.

top_temples.name: Sant Nivruttinath Maharaj Samadhi Mandir
top_temples.location_note: Within Trimbak town; samadhi (1219 CE) of Nivruttinath, elder brother and guru of Sant Dnyaneshwar, a major Varkari pilgrimage stop.

top_temples.name: Tulja Bhavani Temple
top_temples.location_note: Tuljapur, Dharashiv district; one of the 51 Shakti Peethas, built by the Kadamb dynasty around the 12th century, revered by the Maratha royal family.

top_temples.name: Ghatshila Temple
top_temples.location_note: In Tuljapur town; associated with the legend of Rama and Lakshmana's search for Sita, and Goddess Bhavani showing them the way.
